children: One of Asia's largest hedge funds, Aspex Management, posted a loss of about 16% in October when a selloff in AI-linked stocks rattled global markets, a person with knowledge of the matter said.
It marked one of the biggest monthly drawdowns for the $14 billion Hong Kong-based fund, according to the source.
But the fund, focused on pan-Asian equities, is still up 9% this year through October, the source said.
Aspex Management, founded by former Och-Ziff Capital Management Asia equities head Hermes Li, did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.
During October, investors dumped AI-related stocks from chipmakers to hyperscalers amid ‌growing skepticism about whether they will gain sufficient returns from massive investments in the sector.
dropped 5%, while in Asia, the tech-heavy Korean KOSPI index
lost 16% and 6% respectively. The Star 50 index
, a gauge of China's high-tech firms, slumped 24%.
The selloff has gained momentum this month after big wins for the Democrats in the US midterm elections fuelled fears of more regulatory scrutiny for the industry.
Asia was the worst-performing region last month among the equity long-short hedge funds tracked by Goldman Sachs. Asian stock pickers fell 8.3% on average, compared to a 2.5% decline globally.
Aspex has been an active cornerstone investor in Hong Kong listings this year, and was among the backers of AI startup MiniMax
and optical transceiver company Zhongji Innolight
